Thanks Samantha — appreciate the clear list. Short answers below; attaching a reference diagram and a short bullet memo for SIG/CAIQ intake.

- Data residency: Yes — for Private deployments and Dedicated clusters we support pinning the data plane (model weights, KV caches, customer data, and token logs) to an EU region (typically eu-west-1) at customer request. We will provide an attestation letter for production tenancy.
- Control plane: Our hosted control plane operates primarily from us-east-1. The control plane handles orchestration metadata and billing/identity flows. No plaintext customer content is stored in the control plane when Private/Dedicated is selected; only resource and routing metadata is present.
- Telemetry/metadata: Minimal orchestration metadata (instance IDs, model version references, scheduling events) may traverse the control plane. We do not transmit model input/output or secret materials to the control plane for Private deployments.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS is supported (bring-your-own-key). KMS calls can be routed via private endpoints where supported by the cloud region.
- Connectivity: For Private deployments we provide PrivateLink/VPC peering options and explicit support for no-public-egress designs. Customers can require all egress to traverse their VPC NAT/inspection points.
- Audit logs: Default retention for request-level audit logs is 90 days. We offer extended retention (custom agreements) up to 3 years for Dedicated/Private under enterprise contracts.

Attaching: redwood-vpc-architecture-diagram.pdf (diagram), medsys-sig-extract-answers.xlsx (pre-filled answers). Lauren — can you add the short attestation paragraph and a signature block for Marcus?

Best,

Hi Samantha — attaching the short attestation text below (ready for Marcus' sign-off). I've also included a brief technical note on network flows for your engineering team.

--- Attestation (for inclusion in SIG/CAIQ) ---
Redwood Inference confirms that, when configured as a Private deployment or Dedicated cluster for MedSys Health, the customer data plane (model artifacts, token-level logs, KV cache entries, and request payloads) can be operated solely within the EU region (eu-west-1). The hosted control plane for our managed service remains in us-east-1 and is limited to orchestration metadata; Redwood does not persist customer plaintext inputs/outputs in the control plane for Private/Dedicated deployments. Customer-managed KMS is supported and may be used to encrypt at-rest keys.

Network controls: PrivateLink and VPC peering are supported; no public IPs are required on compute instances. Audit logs are retained for 90 days by default; extended retention terms are available under enterprise agreements.

--- Technical note (engineering) ---
- Control plane ↔ data plane: control plane performs model selection and scheduling; payload routing to the EU data plane is via encrypted tunnels (TLS) and can be confined to provider internal backbones where available.
- KMS: BYOK supported; KMS traffic can be routed via private endpoints.
- Egress: customers can enforce VPC-level egress controls; we support forced egress through customer-managed proxies/NAT.

Marcus — please confirm sign-off language below. If you want a CEO-level signature we can run through Legal for a formal attestation letter.

Thanks,
